sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Malta.
Malta is a small, sunny and historic country
in Southern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Malta?
Malta is in the Mediterranean Sea.
It is south of Italy, east of Tunisia and north of Libya.
Malta is made of three main islands.
Malta, the largest island.
Gozo, a quiet island.
Camino, very small with blue water.
What is the capital city of Malta?
The capital city is Valletta.
It is one of the smallest capital cities in Europe.
Valletta has old buildings, churches, museums and harbors.
Other towns include Medina, the old capital,
very quiet and historic.
Sleema and St. Julian's, popular with tourists.
Victoria, the capital of Gozo.
How many people live in Malta?
About 500,000 people live in Malta.
Most people live on the main island.
Malta is small but very full of life.
Many people speak more than one language
and tourism is a big part of life.
What language do people speak in Malta?
The two official languages are
Maltese, the national language,
based on Arabic, Italian and English.
English, widely spoken in schools and government.
Some people also speak Italian.
Many signs and menus are in two or three languages.
What is the weather like in Malta?
Malta has a Mediterranean climate, hot, dry summers,
mild rainy winters.
It is sunny most of the year and the sea is warm in summer.
Many people go swimming, boating or sunbathing.
What does Malta look like?
Malta has rocky beaches and cliffs,
blue water and harbors, stone buildings and narrow streets,
temples, castles and forts.
There are also green fields but no big forests or rivers.
What animals live in Malta?
Malta does not have many wild animals
but you can find lizards, hedgehogs and rabbits,
birds, especially in spring and autumn,
fish, crabs and octopus in the sea.
Many people have cats and dogs as pets.
What do people eat in Malta?
Maltese food is a mix of Mediterranean and Arab flavors.
People eat bread, pasta and rice,
fish, rabbit and beef, tomatoes, peas, beans and olives,
popular dishes, pastizzi, small pastries filled with cheese
or peas, rabbit stew, a national dish,
fattira, Maltese bread with toppings,
aljada, fish soup with garlic and rice,
incarette, sweet date cakes.
What do people drink in Malta?
People drink water and fruit juice, tea and coffee,
soft drinks.
Adults may drink wine, beer or kenny,
a local bitter orange soda Maltese wine
is often homemade and shared at meals.
What is life like in Malta?
Life in Malta is relaxed, sunny and friendly.
People enjoy eating outside with family and friends,
going to the beach, walking in old towns,
watching fireworks and festivals,
dancing and listening to music.
Many people are Catholic and church life is important.
What are some holidays and traditions in Malta?
Independence Day, September 21st.
Feast days, village celebrations for saints
with lights and music, carnival with costumes and parades,
Christmas with lights, food and church services,
Easter with processions and special bread.
There are many festivals.
People love to celebrate with food and fireworks.
Some fun facts about Malta.
Malta is one of the smallest countries in the world.
It has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The Maltese Cross is a famous symbol.
The megalithic temples are older than the pyramids.
Many movies were filmed in Malta,
like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
Now you know many things about Malta.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the sea, the cities and the traditions.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Maltese, Saka.
